references.text: The continuation of the description of the robe's hem, where golden bells and pomegranates are to alternate around the entire edge.
The fulfillment of the command to make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn on the robe's hem, together with golden bells.
The same materials are mentioned: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, which were to be used for the sanctuary's furnishings.
Blue, purple, and scarlet yarn are also used in the tabernacle's curtain fabrics, the same colors as on the high priest's robe hem.
Blue yarn is also used on the tassels at the corners of garments as a reminder of the Lord's commands.
Pomegranates as decoration are also found on the pillars in Solomon's temple, a similar decorative motif.
Pomegranates are mentioned as a symbol of beauty, a fruit motif that also adorns the high priest's robe.
The execution of the command: shows that the detailed instruction regarding pomegranates and bells was followed precisely.
The execution of the command: shows that the instruction about bells between pomegranates was followed precisely.
The concrete implementation of the pattern (bell/pomegranate) that was commanded confirms the importance of obedience.
